title: GC Store Device Authorization
description: Wire shapes for device authorization and package delivery between the public hub client and the private server. Source of truth for the boundary. Serialized camelCase; enums kebab-case; timestamps RFC 3339 UTC. The entitlement lease itself is NOT modeled here as JSON: it is a JWS Compact string (RFC 7515) signed with EdDSA (RFC 8037); `leasePayload` below documents its decoded claims. See device-authorization.md.

claim.description: The device claim. `license` is optional — a license-less device with a pending request still reaches authorize to receive `access-pending`. Privacy rule: never carried in a URL/query — body over TLS only.

deviceId.description: Hub-generated, opaque, persisted device identifier (see device-identity-provisioning.md). Paired with license in the DB; the server binds the fingerprint to it at activation.

license.description: Device license key — the identity anchor.

fingerprint.description: Advisory/soft signals (MAC, WMI attributes). Spoofable; never the sole basis for a strong grant.

tpmEk.description: Optional TPM endorsement key public part, when the hub can read it. Enables identity attestation, NOT delivery-key sealing.

capabilities.description: What this device's hub can do. Lets the server pick a compatible key-envelope scheme and a lease-verification key, and fail closed otherwise.

schemes.description: Key-envelope schemes the hub can unwrap, e.g. "tpm-seal-v1", "fingerprint-wrap-v1". The server picks from the intersection with its own set.

canSealTpm.description: The hub can seal/unseal a key to this device's TPM (strong delivery binding). Distinct from hasTpmEk.

hasTpmEk.description: The hub can read the TPM EK public key (identity attestation). Does NOT imply canSealTpm.

trustedKeyIds.description: Lease-verification keyIds embedded in this device's installed hub release. The server MUST sign the lease with a keyId in this set (self-negotiating rotation).

authorizeRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/authorize (also the renewal call).

accessRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/access-request — a machine with no license asking for store access (a-posteriori path). Server stores it as 'requested' for manual approval.

email.description: Requester email — where the license key is sent on approval.

fingerprint.description: Advisory signals, for review and for binding at activation. Optional.

leasePayload.description: Decoded claims of the JWS lease (documentation only — on the wire the lease is a JWS Compact string with an EdDSA signature and a header carrying alg=EdDSA and kid).

sub.description: deviceId — opaque, server-assigned; NOT the license key. The hub checks it against the identity it resolves locally (anti-replay).

iat.description: Issued-at (epoch seconds). The hub's last-trusted-time anchor.

exp.description: Renewal horizon (epoch seconds) = earliest paid notAfter. Omitted when all entitlements are perpetual. Reaching it means 'refresh needed', not 'all entitlements end'.

state.description: The hub launches an app only when granted and (if notAfter present) still within validity.

notAfter.description: Per-app hard cutoff (epoch seconds). ABSENT = perpetual (free/device-only). Present = expiring (paid).

deliveryResponse.description: Body of a successful POST /v1/delivery/{appId}. An ungranted device gets 402/403 with a catalog `offer` instead. `keyEnvelope` is OPTIONAL: absent = clear-phase cleartext package (hub downloads + verifies sha-256 + extracts, no decryption); present = the content key wrapped to this device (hardening pass — hub decrypts before install).

package.description: Pointer to the CIPHERTEXT package. Storage is private and non-listable.

url.description: Short-lived, single-use signed URL to the ciphertext. Expires in minutes. No PII in the URL.

expiresAt.description: When the signed URL stops working.

hash.description: Integrity check for the downloaded ciphertext.

keyEnvelope.description: The content key wrapped to this device. The wrapping/sealing METHOD is private server logic; only this shape is on the wire. Lifetime is device-bound, not time-bound (decoupled from package.url).

scheme.description: Chosen from capabilities.schemes ∩ server, e.g. "tpm-seal-v1". Versioned; server fails closed on no overlap.

binding.description: tpm: only this device's TPM can unseal (strong). fingerprint: soft, device-derived (spoofable).

wrappedKey.description: Base64 content key, wrapped so only this device can unwrap.
